subject: Partner commission slabs, lead protection, and ops handoff — ClearPath Consulting
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@clearpath.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-21T16:12:00Z
Subject: Intro: commission structure and lead protection (ClearPath)

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for taking this. Quick context: ClearPath is evaluating a reseller/consulting partnership model where we would bring implementation and integration services for Redwood customers in the Healthcare vertical. Before we run the exec sponsor workshop next week we need clarity on two things so our CFO and channel lead can sign off:

1) Commission slab framework (upfront vs renewal splits, accelerators for exceed thresholds)
2) Lead protection / registration process (how ClearPath registers opportunities and how long we keep exclusivity)

I attached a simple commission table we usually start from (CP_OpenComm_Attachment_Table.xlsx). High level asks from our side:
- A meaningful upfront commission for new ACV (to fund delivery)
- A 90–120 day sales-prospect protection window post-registration
- Clear ops handoff so we can plan engineering scoping and SOWs without friction

Can you sketch your typical slabs and the registration process? If helpful loop in legal and partner ops — copied Asha (channel ops) here.

Best,
Sam
Sam Lee
Head of Partnerships, ClearPath Consulting
attachments: CP_OpenComm_Attachment_Table.xlsx
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@clearpath.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-21T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro: commission structure and lead protection (ClearPath)

Sam —

Thanks for the doc and context — appreciate the clarity. High-level proposal below (moving fast so we can review in the workshop):

Commission slabs (new ACV):
- Standard: 12% of first-year ACV paid on booking
- Accelerator: 18% for any single customer where ClearPath-sourced net new ACV >= $200k in first 12 months
- Renewal: 8% of renewal ACV (years 2+) paid on renewal booking
- One-time implementation credit: Fixed $7,500 credit per new enterprise deal (applied toward Redwood professional services invoices)

Lead registration / protection:
- Registration via HubSpot referral form (we will share a private registration link) with required evidence (intro email, POC, estimated ACV)
- Protection window: 120 days from acceptance of registration unless Redwood engages and converts earlier; we can consider 90 days on strategic, named accounts with signed NDA/LOI
- Claims: partner must submit request within 14 days of Redwood opportunity creation if contesting attribution; Partner Ops will adjudicate within 7 business days

Ops handoff and timing:
- Once opportunity is qualified (BANT+technical fit) we trigger a Partner Ops intake and book a 60-minute technical scoping call with Redwood SEs within 10 business days
- For commission payment we require signed order and customer invoice; payments processed Net 30 after invoice

I've attached a draft commission table for your review (redwood-commission-proposal_v1.xlsx). Major open items I want to flag: clawback for cancellations (we normally do 60-day clawback), exclusivity definitions for named prospects, and how we treat opportunities introduced by multiple partners.

If this aligns, let's 30 min on Thursday to finalize before your CFO review. I'll loop in Partner Ops to discuss intake flows.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Partnerships — Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-commission-proposal_v1.xlsx

Subject: Re: Intro: commission structure and lead protection (ClearPath)

Karthik —

This is helpful, thanks. A couple quick asks from ClearPath leadership:

- Can we get a commitment to a 90-day exclusivity window for any named prospects we provide a written introduction to (names listed in a registration)? 120 is fine as default but 90 would help our finance modeling.
- For the accelerator threshold, could the $200k be measured as cumulative ARR introduced by ClearPath across 12 months (not necessarily single contract)?
- Please share a sample MSA redline we can run with our legal team (ProcureCorp will help on contracting).

If you can share the annotated MSA and confirm the 90 vs 120 option and cumulative counting for accelerator, we can get internal sign-off this week. Also copied their procurement contact (ProcureCorp Legal) for contracting cadence.

Cheers,
Sam

Karthik / team —

Couple operational clarifications from Partner Ops perspective:

1) Lead registration evidence: require date-stamped intro email + short summary (customer name, estimated ACV, POC). We should accept CRM screenshots if email thread is missing, but require chain of custody.

2) Clawback: 60-day clawback for any refunds or cancellations; if customer cancels within 60 days we recover pro-rated commission from next payout. Exceptions: if cancellation due to Redwood product defect (verified) then no clawback.

3) Multiple partners: first valid registration wins, but if multiple partners provide materially different value (e.g., one did implementation work and another did sales intro) we can split on a case-by-case basis — we should add an arbitration step in Partner Ops to resolve within 10 business days.

4) Escrow for high-value deals: recommend a joint escrow hold for deals > $500k to protect commissions during long procurement cycles. We have a short process doc attached (PartnerOps_LEAD_FLOW.pdf).

I'm happy to surface a short intake checklist to ClearPath during the workshop so they understand what evidence to capture.

Camila Reyes
Manager, Partner Operations — Redwood Inference

- Accelerator: we can measure the $200k threshold as cumulative ClearPath-introduced ACV within a 12-month rolling window.
- Clawback: 60 days, standard exceptions for verified product defects.
